title: Snowball refrigeration of Earth’s crust mimics glacial erosion
title_zh: 雪球式冰川冷却模拟地壳冰川侵蚀
abstract: Glaciation cools the crust by setting its surface temperature to 0°C or well below. During the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, these conditions were in place long enough to cool the entire crustal column. Although crustal thermal history can be deciphered by thermochronology, these data are typically interpreted to record depth changes due to burial or erosion. Thermal models of the crust under Cryogenian boundary conditions predict that thermochronometers were substantially altered in the upper quarter to half of the crust. This Snowball Earth refrigeration, with little to no coeval erosion, may have imparted a cooling signal mimicking up to 3‒5 km of glacial erosion. Rock cooling previously attributed to massive Snowball erosion and linked to the Great Unconformity may instead reflect a great refrigeration of Earth’s crust, with implications for thermochronology across other climate events.
abstract_zh: 冰川通过将表面温度降至0°C或更低来冷却地壳。在冷冻纪的雪球地球冰川期间，这种条件持续足够长的时间，以冷却整个地壳柱。虽然可以通过热年代学解析地壳的热历史，但这些数据通常被解释为记录因埋藏或侵蚀导致的深度变化。基于冷冻纪边界条件的地壳热模型预测，热年代计在地壳上部四分之一至一半被显著改变。雪球地球冷却，几乎没有同期侵蚀，可能产生类似3‒5公里冰川侵蚀的冷却信号。先前归因于大规模雪球侵蚀并与大不整合相关的岩石冷却，可能实际上反映了地壳的大规模冷却，对其他气候事件的热年代学具有重要意义。
